title: Iran says regional bloc backs its two-day plan to reopen Hormuz; US reply still awaited
dek: Abbas Araghchi said ten ECO nations supported Tehran's offer to reopen the strait within 48 hours if Washington meets its conditions. Pakistan says it has passed the plan on and is waiting for an answer.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said on Monday that a ten-nation regional bloc had backed Tehran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the United States accepts its conditions, as Pakistan, which has carried messages between the two sides, said it was still waiting for Washington's reply.

Mr Araghchi was speaking in Islamabad after a meeting of foreign ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), whose members include Pakistan, Turkey, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan. He said the meeting had "expressed hope that this plan would lead to a definitive and comprehensive ceasefire", according to reports. There was no immediate confirmation from the other governments that they had endorsed the plan, and no reference to it was reported in the documents the meeting adopted.

## What Iran is offering

Tehran's conditions are the release of Iranian assets frozen abroad, sanctions relief and an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, according to reports. Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has said Iran sent seven conditions through a Qatari mediator, including a formal declaration that the war is over. Iran had earlier offered to reopen the strait within seven days; it has now cut that to two, which Iranian negotiators called a sign of good will, reports said.

Pakistan's deputy prime minister and foreign minister, Ishaq Dar, said both versions had been "extracted" from a memorandum of understanding signed in Islamabad on 18 June. "So, the response from the United States is pending. We have not given up hope or efforts," he told reporters, adding that he hoped Washington would respond "very soon" now that the US midterm elections were over. Mr Araghchi also met Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, in Rawalpindi, according to an account he posted; Pakistan's military did not issue a readout.

The Trump administration has so far called Iran's demands "unacceptable", according to reports. US Vice-President JD Vance said in a television interview on Monday that the administration would not let the conflict become "a 10- or 15-year commitment or, frankly, even a two-year commitment", and that President Donald Trump "has a lot of options".

## The situation at sea

The plan comes as incidents in and around the strait continue. Iran's navy said on Monday that a tanker had hit a naval mine and caught fire, which it called the fourth such incident in 24 hours, according to reports. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) separately reported a vessel disabled by an engine-room fire after an attack north of Khasab in Oman, with the crew safe. None of Iran's claims of ships sunk has been independently confirmed. The US now has three aircraft carriers in the region and says it is enforcing its blockade of Iranian ports.

Iran also said it would not let UN nuclear inspectors into its damaged nuclear sites until its conditions are met. "We will not grant the IAEA access to the facilities until Iran's conditions are met and the war has permanently ended," Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in a televised interview, according to reports.

The war began on 28 February with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. Brent crude was trading at about $95 a barrel on Monday, against about $72 in late February before the war, according to reports.

## Why it matters for India

India imports much of its crude oil and cooking gas from the Gulf, and Indian ships and seafarers use the strait every day. A reopening would ease pressure on fuel prices and on the rupee, which has been trading near 94 to the dollar. On Sunday, Indian shipping authorities reported an attack on a tanker in the Gulf just before the strait; the crew were safe, UKMTO said.

## What happens next

Washington has not said when, or whether, it will respond formally. Mr Trump travels from Manila to Shenzhen for a meeting with China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, where the war with Iran is expected to be discussed, according to reports.
